news.body:
Breakdown: Creating KPop Demon Hunters' Airplane Sequence
The film is now available in a director-approved 4K UHD edition from Criterion.
Produced by Sony Pictures Animation for Netflix, KPop Demon Hunters quickly became a worldwide hit, winning awards, topping music charts, and capturing audiences with its amazing animation, memorable characters, and catchy songs. It's definitely not a film you'll forget anytime soon, and now fans can enjoy it in a director-approved 4K UHD edition featuring a Dolby Atmos soundtrack from Criterion.
As part of Criterion's new 4K release, you can also check out a special feature breaking down the film's opening scene, created by Taylor Ramos and Tony Zhou, the duo behind Every Frame a Painting. The airplane sequence plays an important role in the film, introducing the whole idea of K-pop stars who are also demon hunters and love to eat. In this video, key members of the crew break down how the sequence came together, from the first draft to the final mix.
Here's what else you can expect from the director-approved 4K UHD + Blu-ray Special Edition of KPop Demon Hunters:
- A full feature-length animatic, with a new introduction by Kang and Appelhans
- A new making-of documentary
- An additional visual essay by Taylor Ramos & Tony Zhou on the film’s use of music
- Lyric videos for seven of the songs in the film, including How It's Done
- Collectible postcards featuring original illustrations by artists who worked on the film
- A new cover by Ami Thompson
Learn more here. If you're looking for more behind-the-scenes content from KPop Demon Hunters, check out this article for breakdowns covering how Rumi was animated, how the film's VFX were created, and how the team brought Seoul to life.

news.title: Report: Silver Lake and the Saudi Arabia PIF hold talks with Unity to explore acquisition
news.summary_raw: The investment partners recently acquired Electronic Arts and are now reportedly turning their gaze toward software engine Unity.

members.title: Report: Silver Lake and the Saudi Arabia PIF hold talks with Unity to explore acquisition
Silver Lake & PIF Are Reportedly Talking about Buying Unity
Unity reportedly in acquisition talks with Silver Lake and Public Investment Fund, two firms involved in EA's $55bn buyout

news.body:
Unity Software, the company behind the Unity game engine, is in conversations with Silver Lake and the Saudi Arabia Private Investment Fund, according to new reporting from Reuters. Both Silver Lake and the PIF just recently finalized an acquisition of Electronic Arts, taking the company private in a leveraged buyout.
The Reuters story states that a consortium of investors are involved, with the biggest being Silver Lake—owned by United States President Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner—and Saudi Arabia's Private Investment Fund, which has been investing in numerous video game and technology companies internationally. Silver Lake already owns eight percent of Unity, but Reuters reports that PIF approached both Unity and the investment firm to make an offer for a full buyout.
The sources for the Reuters report also state that the deal would take the form of a leveraged buyout, much like the Electronic Arts deal which purchased the company with funds that would need to be recouped by its operating profit. While not being the record-breaking numbers the EA acquisition boasted, this would still be one of the biggest leveraged buyouts in history.
Unity's game engine is used, by their own accounting, in over half of all mobile games and a large proportion of console and PC games. Scopely, which is already owned by the PIF and Silver Lake among others, uses it to power titles like Pokémon Go and Monopoly Go.
Unity has expanded to an AI-prominent structure, recently launching a prompt-based tool in collaboration with Google to create games entirely from user prompts called Unity Spark.
The company unveiled a new policy of Runtime Fees in 2024 which was intended to charge developers a per-install tariff, but a monumental backlash to the idea from developers forced Unity to undo the planned policy. Declining stock prices were perhaps the reason then-Unity CEO John Riccitiello—also former CEO of Electronic Arts—resigned from his position. The current CEO, Matthew Bromberg, was also a former EA executive who acted as General Manager of BioWare, a studio which the publisher recently shut down as it attempts to pay off the leveraged buyout from Silver Lake and PIF.
The backlash that unseated Riccitiello shows that Unity is not inured to revolt from its client-facing business, unlike Electronic Arts which does not deal directly with individual developers at a similar scale. A buyout from new, controversial owners could lead to an upheaval in Unity's core business, potentially putting the company's operating profit at risk.

members.title: 从“资金支持”到“全球发行”：索尼“中国之星计划”第四期媒体群访
索尼“中国之星计划 ” 第四期招募中，单项目将获价值百万美元投资

news.body:
2026年11月3日，索尼互动娱乐在上海举办了“中国之星计划”发布会，正式公布了第四期计划的最新进展。
自2016年启动以来，中国之星计划已经走过十年，累计选拔了19款国产游戏，其中11款已经正式上市。作为PlayStation扶持中国本土游戏开发者的重要项目，中国之星计划也在不断调整自己的支持方式，尝试为开发团队提供从游戏开发、发行到市场推广等更加全面的帮助。
在此次发布会上，最受关注的变化无疑是第四期支持力度的进一步升级：索尼互动娱乐将为每个入选项目提供价值100万美元的项目投资，同时引入DENMU電夢和Solutions 2 GO两家新的战略合作伙伴，希望从资金、开发支持以及全球发行等不同层面，为中国开发者提供更多帮助。与此同时，第三期入选作品《绝晓》也将获得价值100万美元的追加投资，而《达巴：水痕之地》与《潜阈限界》则分别公布了2027年的发售计划。
从最初的项目选拔，到如今逐渐形成包含投资机构、发行商在内的合作网络，中国之星计划正在尝试构建一套更加完整的国产游戏孵化体系。但对于开发者来说，资金和资源的增加究竟意味着什么？在国产单机游戏逐渐受到全球市场关注的今天，开发团队又该如何找到自己的特色，并真正具备面向全球市场的竞争力？
带着这些问题，我们在发布会结束后，与索尼互动娱乐中国区游戏制作总监包波、《绝晓》游戏制作人应超、DENMU電夢管理合伙人兼CEO游镕畅，以及Solutions 2 GO Asia副总裁片方祐介进行了交流。从中国之星计划的投资与孵化逻辑，到国产游戏的创作方向和海外市场的机会，四位受访者也分享了各自的观察与判断。
Q1. 中国之星计划第四期的一项重要升级，是为每款入选游戏提供100万美元的资金支持。为什么选择在当前这个时间节点推出这样的投资？这笔资金希望为开发团队带来怎样的帮助？
包波： PlayStation 增加对项目的投资，在一定程度上也是对作品的一种背书。这能够帮助开发团队吸引更多投资人、发行商以及其他优质合作伙伴，这才是我们最主要的目的。
当然，PlayStation 的投资也能够在短时间内帮助团队解决一部分实际问题。至于经济回报，我们内部的要求其实比较少，更多还是希望能够尽自己的一份力量，支持中国开发者成长。
Q2. 对于开发团队来说，100万美元的投资具体能够解决哪些问题？
应超： 100万美元肯定不是一笔小钱。甚至在过去，对于一些独立游戏来说，单款游戏的制作成本可能只需要100万美元。当然，如果是2A、3A规模的产品，肯定还需要更多资金支持。
以目前国内的投资环境来看，单笔100万美元也不是一个小数目，能够帮助团队解决很多实际问题。另外，由索尼互动娱乐来进行这笔投资，和单纯获得一笔资金的意义还是不太一样的。这也代表着行业内一位经验丰富的前辈对团队的认可，这一点同样非常有帮助。
Q3. 在中国之星计划的商业化过程中，索尼互动娱乐及其合作伙伴会为入选团队提供哪些支持？例如，Solutions 2 GO 负责全球发行与推广，具体会如何帮助中国开发者在国际市场上获得更好的商业回报？
片方祐介： Solutions 2 GO 首先是一家全球化公司，我们在北美、南美以及亚洲都有自己的分公司。这意味着我们在不同市场都有熟悉当地情况的专业团队，能够更加准确地了解当地用户和玩家的需求与痛点，再根据不同市场的特点制定相应的宣传推广策略。
另一方面，以我自己作为日本游戏玩家的经验来说，我对游戏本土化的要求非常高，包括语言翻译是否准确、表达是否自然，以及整体内容能否被日本玩家接受。因此，在本土化方面，Solutions 2 GO 也能够为开发团队提供帮助，包括翻译校对、内容确认等工作。
Q4. 中国之星计划提供的100万美元，具体是以项目投资的形式进行，还是会涉及股权投资？
Q5. 電夢主要从事游戏投资。目前市场上专注于游戏领域的美元基金并不多，为什么你们仍然选择专注于游戏这个赛道？
游镕畅： 游戏市场每年的收入规模大约有2000亿美元，和其他市场相比，它一点也不小，实际上是一个非常庞大的产业。但在金融市场上，游戏行业给人的感觉却相对比较小。
我认为，游戏行业本身的金融属性、财务属性与传统金融市场之间存在很多不契合的地方。虽然游戏市场规模很大，也是最重要的文化产业之一，但如果用传统投资VC或者科技公司的方式来投资游戏，很难获得和科技行业类似的回报。
我们一直在思考如何解决这个问题。游戏行业同样需要持续的资金投入，因此我们选择只投资游戏。从基金结构、交易设计到整体架构和团队配置，我们都是围绕游戏行业的特点来设计的。我们希望为基金投资人提供一种不同于AI或者其他传统金融投资领域的回报，我们称之为“Uncorrelated Return”（非相关性回报）。从这个角度来说，游戏是一个非常有趣的投资领域。
当然，开个玩笑来说，投资其他行业的人已经很多了，但我们觉得游戏行业仍然有大量值得探索的事情。最后还有一个很重要的原因，就是我们确实很喜欢游戏。我一直觉得，人还是应该做自己喜欢的事情。
Q6. 过去中国之星计划曾经提出过“好玩、好看、好听”的项目选拔标准。但到了2026年，随着虚拟制作技术的普及以及AI工具的应用，玩家对国产3A游戏的期待似乎也在不断提高。如今，这套标准是否发生了变化？
包波： 游戏项目的选拔其实是一个非常复杂的过程。如果单纯从投资回报的角度考虑，投资大型项目可能是更稳妥的选择。但中国之星计划从一开始就选择支持中小型开发团队，因此它更偏向于孵化，同时也承担着改善开发环境、建设开发者社区的责任。
所以，我们对投资回报的要求没有那么高，更希望能够帮助国产游戏开发团队提升整体水平。只有市场上高水平的团队越来越多，彼此之间形成良性竞争，优秀的作品才有机会不断涌现。
这两年，玩家们接触过的优秀游戏越来越多，尤其是《黑神话：悟空》。包括这两天我也一直在玩《影之刃零》，确实做得非常不错。这些游戏的投资规模都比较高，虽然还不能和海外那些顶级项目相比，但在国内已经属于投资规模相当大的项目了。通常来说，这样的投资规模也能够为作品的品质提供一定保障。
我们要做的事情，其实是培养开发团队，让他们逐渐掌握如何管理和使用更大规模的资金。一个团队在获得1000万美元投资时，能不能把这1000万美元花好，最终做出符合这个投资规模的高质量产品？即使大家拿到同样的1000万美元，最后呈现出来的品质也可能有很大差距。
我们能够提供的帮助，就是让团队逐渐建立起更加成熟的工业化流程，积累更多开发经验。游戏研发本身并不逊色于高科技项目，因为它涉及大量人员协作，程序、美术等领域也都在使用尖端技术。我们需要依靠经验和效率，不断提升团队管理水平，把游戏当作高标准的产品来制作。
只有这样，团队未来才有可能进一步扩大规模，并具备驾驭更高额度投资的能力。当团队能够合理使用大规模投资，并且取得不错的市场回报时，大家才不会觉得这些钱被浪费了。无论是丰富的游戏内容、高品质的美术表现，还是出色的战斗演出和大量动画，都可以成为这种投入的具体体现。
所以，中国之星计划最重要的目标，就是帮助本土团队成长，让他们具备承担更大规模项目的能力，同时也能够把手里的资金使用好。在技术之外，我们还会寻找不同的合作伙伴，例如Denmu 電夢和Solutions 2 GO，帮助这些团队走向海外市场。
游镕畅： 我认为，中国游戏过去十年的发展，主要是以提升“质量”为核心。所谓质量，在很大程度上其实是在对标工业化，因为过去中国单机游戏并没有完整的工业化基础。现在这方面虽然还没有完全成熟，但在各方面的帮助下，已经有了很大的进步。
不过，我认为如今游戏市场并不缺少产品供给，真正稀缺的还是有趣、有特色的作品。
可能在五年或者十年前，一款游戏只要打出“中国2A”或者“中国3A”的概念，就能够获得市场关注。但这个阶段很快就会过去。接下来，游戏还是需要找到自己的特色。质量好只是一个基本要求，而不是全部。相反，一些规模较小的产品，即使在制作质量上没有那么突出，只要足够有特色，同样有机会获得市场认可。
Q7. 中国之星计划一直将自身定位为游戏孵化项目。过去几年，你们是否讨论过调整计划的定位？还是说从一开始就确定了孵化方向，并希望在这个基础上不断深化？
包波： 中国之星计划本身就是一个带有选拔性质的孵化项目，我们只会孵化自己认为有潜力的项目，这是一个前提。
一个项目能不能成功，我认为有两个关键点：第一，它必须能够顺利完成开发；第二，它最终的品质必须足够好。在商业表现方面，最基本的要求是，它至少不能明显落后于同类型产品。只有达到这样的标准，我们才会考虑支持。
中国之星计划支持的项目并没有规模限制。我们希望找到真正优秀的项目，只要它在同类产品中具备竞争力，我们就愿意帮助它成长。
所以，我们仍然会专注于孵化，只不过在项目选择上会保持严格的标准。
Q8. 目前中国游戏市场的环境正在发生变化，各种规模、不同品质的产品不断涌现。作为合作伙伴，你们在与中国之星计划合作时，最看重它在哪些方面的优势？为什么认为双方的合作能够形成互补？
游镕畅： 我认为，我们和索尼互动娱乐的中国之星计划非常契合。
因为在中国市场，我们接触过很多项目，其中有大量非常优秀的创意，但真正能够把创意落地成一款完整游戏的项目却并不多。我相信未来这种情况会逐渐改善，但在现阶段，对于投资人来说，一个项目可能有很好的想法、很出色的创意，甚至已经有了表现不错的Demo，但从这些内容到最终完成一款游戏，中间仍然存在很大的难度。
而中国之星计划能够在这方面提供帮助，这让我们没有太多后顾之忧。我们可以把更多注意力放在游戏本身的亮点、市场定位以及它能够带给玩家怎样的乐趣上，而不用过多担心具体制作环节的问题。
片方祐介： 中国之星计划已经帮助我们完成了第一轮项目筛选，所以来到我们这里的项目，基本上都已经经过了一定程度的品质验证，这一点让我们比较安心。
另外，项目既然能够入选中国之星计划，就意味着它会获得索尼互动娱乐相当大的支持。包括后续游戏上市以及宣传推广等方面，都有机会得到PlayStation的帮助。例如通过State of Play获得曝光，对我们来说也是非常重要的支持。
Q9. 中国之星计划为入选游戏提供100万美元的投资，这是否会进一步增强合作伙伴对项目的信心？
游镕畅： 100万美元对于不同规模的项目来说，占整体预算的比例可能有很大差别。但我们和索尼互动娱乐有过很多合作，PlayStation对于项目投资一直都非常慎重。因此，当PlayStation愿意为一个项目投资100万美元时，这本身就是一种非常重要的背书。对于我们这些合作伙伴来说，这会显著增强对项目的信心。
片方祐介： 如果是得到中国之星计划支持的游戏，在中国市场进行宣传推广时，索尼互动娱乐肯定也会提供相应帮助。这能够让游戏获得更多关注和人气。日本市场其实也会关注这一点。日本玩家和发行商会在意一款游戏在中国市场是否受到欢迎、是否拥有一定人气，这些因素都会对他们的判断产生影响。
Q10. 在Denmu 電夢接触不同游戏项目的过程中，开发者和投资方对于一款游戏的关注点是否会存在错位？
游镕畅： 总体来说，我们的目标是一致的，只不过每个人都会从自己的角度去看待一款游戏。很多时候，开发者会完全从自己团队的角度出发，去理解和评价自己的作品，因此可能会忽略一些来自市场的看法。但反过来说，如果一味地按照市场反馈来制作游戏，也很难做出足够独特的作品。所以，最后其实是一个不断协调和平衡的过程。
在和开发者沟通时，我们首先会了解他们自己是如何看待这款游戏的，然后再以此为基础，评估他们对游戏特色和方向的判断是否合理。
我们也会为开发团队带来更多外部视角。因为在开发过程中，团队非常需要持续获得外界的反馈，形成一个比较完整的反馈循环。但这件事其实并不容易，因为当你向亲朋好友或者业内朋友征求意见时，对方往往不太愿意直接指出问题。
而我们作为和开发者利益共担的合作伙伴，就可以更加直接地表达自己的看法。当然，开发团队可以选择接受，也可以选择不接受，但我认为，能够提供这样的反馈本身就是非常重要的。
Q11. 《绝晓》作为中国之星计划第三期的入选项目，在加入计划之后，团队与索尼互动娱乐经历了怎样的合作过程？如今获得100万美元的投资，又会对接下来的开发产生哪些实际影响？是否有一些过去受限于资源和预算、不得不暂缓的想法，现在有机会重新考虑？
应超： 入选中国之星计划之后，我们经历了很多合作与配合的节点。我们会定期提交不同版本，中国之星计划的团队会帮助我们进行评估，同时也有音频、音效等支持部门为我们提供帮助，包括组织试玩活动。
2024年和2025年，我们都曾经在ChinaJoy的PlayStation展台上提供线下试玩。这些活动是我们接触玩家、收集反馈的重要机会，也让我们获得了很多有价值的意见。
游戏已经开发了很多年，在这个过程中，团队自然会产生大量想法。但最终，我们还是需要能够快速地向玩家介绍这款游戏究竟是什么，它最核心的特点是什么。因此，在现阶段，我们要做的并不是继续发散，而是进行收敛。
我们不会因为获得了投资，就想着额外增加更多内容。现阶段的核心目标，还是把过去两三年里通过玩家试玩，以及与业内朋友交流所收集到的反馈进行提炼，将其中最重要的内容融入游戏。
我们希望制作的并不是一个规模庞大、面面俱到的顶级豪华盛宴，而是先把最精华的内容和最核心的品质打磨好。这才是接下来最重要的事情。
Q12. 《绝晓》此次获得追加资金支持，在重新评估项目时，索尼互动娱乐重点看到了哪些变化？是团队开发实力的提升，还是项目展现出了新的潜力？
包波： 关于这个项目的投资，我们其实已经沟通了很长时间，此次正式公布投资，只是整个过程中的一个后置环节。《绝晓》团队的开发能力和开发速度都是我们比较认可的，同时这个项目本身也足够独特。
我们的投资评估是一个综合性的过程，而且会持续进行。比如，我们会交换不同阶段的游戏版本，了解团队的开发计划、资金安排和人员配置等情况，也会比较频繁地与开发团队、项目投资人以及其他合作伙伴进行沟通。
Q13. 这次加入中国之星计划，Solutions 2 GO 看中了中国游戏市场的哪些潜力？结合你们在海外市场的经验，希望从中国开发团队身上找到什么样的作品？
片方祐介： 从目前整个游戏市场的发展趋势来看，包括《黑神话：悟空》和《影之刃零》，这些中国游戏在海外市场都获得了非常好的反响，也受到了很多玩家的关注。因此，我们希望在这两款作品之后，能够继续从中国市场发现更多优秀的游戏。
刚才大家也提到了《达巴：水痕之地》。这款游戏的背景取材于中国西域文化。由于日本和中国在文化上有一些相通的地方，其中涉及的部分文化元素对我们来说也并不陌生。
此前我们也和游戏开发团队交流过。当时听他们介绍游戏背景和相关内容时，我感触很深。他们准备了大量资料，而我们现在看到的可能还只是其中的冰山一角。如果能够将这些资料中的亮点和创作想法更好地传递给海外玩家，那将是一件非常好的事情。
包波： 《达巴：水痕之地》主要取材于中国西域文化，其中涉及西藏、新疆、内蒙古、宁夏以及陕西等不同地区的文化元素。开发团队为了这些内容，曾经在全国各地进行采风，花费了相当长的时间，最终才逐渐沉淀出游戏中的内容。
这款游戏的内核其实是一个非常中国式的故事，具有鲜明的中国文化特色。我们也期待之后能够和大家分享更多相关信息。
Q14. 今年市场上受到关注的国产单机游戏，大多集中在动作游戏或者ARPG领域。这既与国内团队的技术积累有关，也与市场需求有关。从中国之星计划的项目扶持，以及投资合作伙伴的角度来看，你们会更倾向于选择已经得到市场验证的游戏类型，还是愿意承担风险，支持一些新的类型和创意？
游镕畅： 我们投资过《星球大战：银河赛车手》。这是一个星球大战题材的赛车游戏，没有绝地武士，也没有光剑，只有赛车。当时我们决定投资时，很多人觉得我们是不是疯了。
确实有不少人认为这款游戏的市场定位存在问题：喜欢星球大战的人未必喜欢赛车，而喜欢赛车的人也未必关注星球大战。但最终的市场表现大家也可以看到，这款游戏获得了不少认可。
所以，我们并不是采用一种自上而下的投资理念，并不是觉得某个游戏类型比较热门，就只投资这个类型。我们更关注的是，一款产品能不能呈现出足够独特的幻想，这种幻想是否足够吸引人，以及游戏本身的体量能否支撑起这样的创意。
至于为什么中国目前出现了这么多动作游戏，我认为这和产业发展的阶段有关。相对来说，动作游戏更容易在视觉和表现层面做出比较突出的效果，也更容易让玩家直观地感受到品质。
因此，我觉得现阶段大家选择动作游戏没有问题。但从长远来看，开发者肯定会希望探索更多不同的方向，我们也相信中国游戏在这方面会有很大的发展空间。
Q15. 中国之星计划会为开发团队提供具体建议，但同时也会尊重开发者自己的创作理念。在实际合作过程中，例如与《绝晓》团队的合作，双方是否出现过对游戏设计存在不同看法的情况？如果有，又是如何处理的？
包波： 对于合作项目，我们如果发现某些地方做得不好，一定会直接提出意见。比如，我们可能会告诉开发团队，游戏的打击感不够好，震动、音效和动画之间的配合还不到位。
但开发者始终是项目的主体，具体要如何修改，或者是否需要修改，最终还是由他们自己决定。如果开发者认为有更适合自己的解决方式，我们通常也会尊重他们的想法，因为他们才是一线的操作者和执行者。《绝晓》本身是一个很好的项目，我们能够提出的意见其实没有那么多。不过，未来我们可能还会针对手柄震动等方面给出一些建议，因为PlayStation一直非常重视手柄反馈。
开发者往往有自己独特的设计想法，但在实际制作过程中，很难把所有因素都考虑得百分之百周全，这在游戏开发中是很常见的情况。如果我们发现了某些问题，双方团队就会一起讨论如何解决。
我觉得这其实是一个相互学习的过程。比如你很擅长骑自行车，我就可以向你学习；如果我比较擅长打篮球，你也可以跟我学习投篮。合作就是这样一个过程。
游镕畅： 我认为游戏开发团队大致可以分为三种类型。
第一种是无论你提出什么意见，他们都觉得自己没有问题，甚至会和你产生非常激烈的争论。这类团队往往缺乏足够的安全感，过于在意外界的评价，我觉得这不是一种很好的合作状态。
第二种是你提出什么意见，他们都会把它当成圣旨一样去执行。这同样不理想，因为这样做出来的游戏，最终可能就不再是开发者自己的作品了。
第三种是我认为比较理想的团队：他们愿意认真听取所有意见，然后结合自己的实际情况，有选择地吸收和应用。
我觉得，一个好的游戏开发团队应该具备这样的能力。听完刚才的分享，我反而对《绝晓》团队更加感兴趣了。
Q16. 受到国产成功作品的影响，越来越多国产游戏开始进入市场。除了美术风格和文化题材之外，作为投资人，你们还会通过哪些方面来判断一款游戏是否具备自己的特色？有没有一些项目最初看起来并不算特别突出，但在实际试玩或者体验Demo之后，让你们改变了看法？
游镕畅： 游戏是一件非常复杂的事情。对于目前的市场来说，视觉表现确实非常重要。你很难想象一款游戏在视觉上完全没有特点，却仅仅依靠其他方面获得市场成功。虽然这种情况并不是不可能，但确实比较少见。所以，我认为视觉一直都是一个重要的因素。
不过，我们不太喜欢把游戏非常客观地拆解成文化、题材或者其他单独的部分来分析。我们更关注的是：你希望通过这款游戏给玩家带来怎样的体验？这种体验是否足够独特？
比如《达巴：水痕之地》，战斗是它的主要体验之一，所以我们会把更多注意力放在战斗上。但对于另外一些游戏来说，它可能希望通过100条不同的剧情线、100种不同的故事体验来吸引玩家，那么战斗在其中所占的比重就没有那么高。
所以，最重要的还是弄清楚这款游戏希望呈现怎样的Fantasy，也就是它希望带给玩家怎样的幻想和体验，以及能不能把这种体验很好地传递出去。这才是我们比较看重的事情。
我认为，目前中国游戏面临的问题，并不是缺乏创意。很多项目第一眼看上去都很不错，但真正玩起来之后，就会发现存在不少问题。
尤其是在Demo阶段，由于体验时间比较短，开发团队往往能够很好地展现自己最想表达的内容。但这些内容能不能支撑起一款完整的游戏，是另外一回事。毕竟一款游戏可能需要玩家投入10个小时甚至20个小时，这和电影是完全不同的。
很多做游戏的人可能希望把游戏做得像电影一样，总是想着向玩家讲述一个故事。但问题在于，游戏有10个小时的体验时间，你不可能一直向玩家讲故事。如何通过玩法本身来讲述故事，同时让玩家在游玩的过程中感到有趣，这是非常困难的。
所以，我认为目前国内游戏比较突出的问题，就是Demo很吸引人，但最终完成的游戏却未必能够达到同样的水平。这才是更值得关注的问题。至于中国游戏缺乏创意，我倒是一点也不担心。
Q17. 中国之星计划这次引入了新的合作伙伴。在挑选合作伙伴时，你们主要依据哪些标准？希望这些合作伙伴为计划带来哪些帮助？
包波： Denmu 電夢和Solutions 2 GO这两家合作伙伴，对于中国之星计划来说都具有很重要的意义。因为我们发现，很多入选项目在开发过程中面临的问题其实比较相似。例如，团队在海外市场能够获得的资源比较少。因此，我们希望引入一些合作伙伴，帮助他们补齐这方面的支持。
另一方面，很多入选项目也需要合作伙伴具备一定的游戏判断能力，能够提供真正有效的反馈。比如Denmu 電夢，他们拥有国际视野，也有专业人员能够从不同角度对游戏进行评价。这种能力非常重要，不仅对我们有帮助，对开发团队来说更是如此。
至于Solutions 2 GO，他们与PlayStation的合作已经超过20年。索尼互动娱乐在全球各地的部分办公室，也是与Solutions 2 GO共同建立的。所以，中国之星计划与Denmu 電夢、Solutions 2 GO展开合作，可以说是水到渠成的事情。
Q18. 回顾中国之星计划的发展历程，如今接触到的项目，以及在推进过程中遇到的困难，与五年前相比发生了哪些变化？站在现在这个时间节点，你们如何看待中国单机游戏行业的发展？
包波： 我觉得国内开发者经历了一个自我发现和自我理解的过程。
首先，国内有很多优秀的人才在大型游戏公司工作，他们已经拥有很高的收入，因此未必愿意离开原来的工作，出来开发单机游戏。
其次，真正热爱单机游戏、愿意投入这个领域的人，可能没有大家想象中那么多。不过，这两年相关人才和团队的数量确实有了明显增长。可能是因为《黑神话：悟空》的成功，让大家看到了国产单机游戏的发展势头，也让越来越多团队开始看好这个领域，愿意出来创业。
但我现在最大的感受是，中国团队的实力确实很强。这次我也专门体验了《影之刃零》，我觉得它已经做得非常好了。再加上我们平时接触到的很多开发团队，有一些目前还没有正式公布的项目，其团队实力绝对会让大家感到惊讶。
我认为，中国开发者一直在努力，整个过程虽然曲折，但总体是在向上发展的。
应超： 对于想要开发单机游戏的人来说，现在的环境肯定比过去好了很多。但如果说国产单机游戏是不是已经进入爆发期，我觉得还没有。大家也可以看看接下来即将推出的项目，真正能够数得出来的其实还是有限的，距离集中收获的阶段还有一段时间。
不过，整体趋势和两年前，甚至一年前相比，已经完全不一样了。我认为整个行业的发展方向是积极的。包括《影之刃零》取得了很好的成绩，我们也非常高兴，这对所有开发者来说都是一种信心上的提振。
游镕畅： 如果要用一个简单的标准来判断中国单机游戏的春天是否真正到来，我认为可以看中国大作在中国市场的营收占比。如果中国大作在中国市场的营收占比能够低于50%，那就说明这个春天真的来了。
我觉得我们距离这一天还有一段路要走。春天可能就要来了，但还没有真正到来。
中国市场当然很大，但世界市场更大。到目前为止，中国游戏对于海外市场、全球市场的探索，其实还处在非常初期的阶段。这里面仍然有大量机会，未来还有很大的发展空间。
片方祐介： 首先，我非常期待那一天的到来，也希望到时候Solutions 2 GO能够参与其中，为中国开发者提供帮助。如果能够为大家尽一份力量，那就再好不过了。另外，我希望未来不仅仅是游戏本身能够取得更好的销售成绩，也希望大家对于单机游戏的看法能够发生变化，让更多

news.title: Our new XR e-book is here: Build XR with Unity: Meta XR
news.summary_raw: Download the free Build XR with Unity: Meta XR e-book. Learn eye and hand tracking, 5K display optimization, and AI-assisted workflows for Meta VR Glasses.

members.title: Our new XR e-book is here: Build XR with Unity: Meta XR

news.body:
Our new XR e-book is here: Build XR with Unity: Meta XR
Eduardo Oriz - Unity Technologies
What's inside the guide
This e-book is for Unity XR developers who want to create a new title or port an existing app to Meta VR devices. Among other things, it explains how to do the following:
- Understand what sets Meta VR Glasses apart: a roughly 100-gram form factor, eye and hand tracking as primary input, and the same OS, store, and OpenXR stack as Quest, so existing Quest apps can run on them.
- Get started with Unity's VR template and test on a device, in the Editor with the XR Interaction Simulator, or with Meta XR Simulator.
- Use key XR Interaction Toolkit components: XR Origin, teleportation, grab interactables, spatial UI, and more.
- Support eye and hand tracking for Look and Pinch input, with fallbacks for users who don't grant eye tracking permission.
- Build a simple interactive VR scene step by step, from Editor setup to deploying on hardware.
- Optimize graphics with gaze-based foveated rendering, Quad Views, Application SpaceWarp, dynamic resolution, and Adaptive Performance.
- Speed up iteration with the new Unity CLI, the Unity Pipeline package, and AI agents.
Continue scrolling for excerpts on the capabilities that Meta VR Glasses unlock, and on an AI-assisted build-test-verify workflow.
Capabilities to go deeper
Meta VR Glasses open up four capabilities for meaningful new experiences:
- Eye Tracking: Supports foveated rendering and gaze input, which can inform both visual quality and interaction design. Eye tracking data is private by default, so your app must request permission. Plan a fallback, such as hand raycasting, for users who decline.
- Quad Views Rendering: Renders each eye’s periphery at lower resolution than the center, cutting GPU cost while maintaining perceived visual quality, giving you more headroom for scene complexity.
- Spatial Audio: Unity supports 7.1.4 surround sound with Enhanced Audio Foundation, enabling Spatial Audio experiences for VR with seven surround channels, four height channels and a low-frequency effects channel. Select 7.1.4 in Output Channel Layout.
- 5K Infinite Display: The 5K Infinite Display uses micro-OLED panels with a per-eye resolution of 2412 x 2288 pixels at 37 PPD, compared with 25 PPD on Quest 3 with a higher contrast. Consider supporting high resolutions when possible to take full advantage of the Meta VR Glasses’ displays.
Get started with Unity's VR template
The VR template, available in the Unity Hub, gives you sample scenes, assets, and recommended packages and settings. The e-book uses Unity 6.6 and XR Interaction Toolkit 3.6, and recommends the same version or newer.
To run the template on a device, enable Developer mode, connect the headset, switch the platform to Meta Quest in File > Build Profiles, and select Build and Run. In Project Settings, check that OpenXR and both the Meta and Android XR feature groups are enabled. That runs the sample on Meta devices and keeps portability to other platforms open.
No headset at hand? The XR Interaction Simulator, part of the XR Interaction Toolkit package, lets you test interactions in the Editor. Windows users can also use Meta Horizon Link to launch the app on a device straight from the Editor, with no build-and-deploy step each time.
Optimize for the 5K display
Meta VR Glasses have more on-chip GPU memory than Meta Quest 3, so the tiled renderer can split each frame into fewer tiles. To use that headroom, the e-book covers:
- Gaze-based foveated rendering: Full resolution where the user is looking, lower elsewhere, with optional dynamic foveation that adjusts as GPU load changes
- Quad Views: Draws the central focus area at full resolution and the periphery at lower resolution
- Application SpaceWarp: Renders fewer frames while the runtime generates intermediate ones from motion and depth data
- Dynamic resolution and Adaptive Performance: Keep render resolution in range and respond to thermal or workload pressure to hold a stable frame rate
If you're porting a Quest 2 or Quest 3 project, reevaluate your foveated rendering approach: fixed foveated rendering returns a smaller saving on Meta VR Glasses. Whichever technique you choose, benchmark your app to confirm what performs best.
Build, test, and verify with Unity CLI and AI agents
Clicking through Editor panels can become a bottleneck for repetitive tasks and automation. The new Unity CLI and Unity Pipeline package give both developers and AI agents a fast, lightweight command-line interface into the Unity Editor. The Pipeline package turns the running Editor into a local background server, so scenes and asset databases stay warm in memory and there's no cold-start boot for every command.
Any agent that can run shell commands, including Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, and Gemini CLI, can control the Editor, build your app, and help fix errors. Unity's official plugins for Claude and Codex teach agents to do jobs the way Unity workflows are meant to work, and install 29 skills with a single command at launch.
To close the loop, Meta XR Operator lets an agent act inside the running XR app: inspect the scene, move the head, controllers, and hands, perform gestures like pinch, poke, and grab (including gaze-and-pinch for Meta VR Glasses), and capture the rendered view to verify the result. It's an experimental component, so use it for development and testing rather than as a production dependency, and keep testing comfort, tracking, and performance on physical hardware.
Download the e-book
Ready to Build for Meta VR Glasses? Download Build XR with Unity: Meta XR to get the full step-by-step walkthrough, including the interactive scene tutorial and links to samples, video tutorials, and Unity Learn resources.

news.title: How SEED renders a world players never stop building

members.title: How SEED renders a world players never stop building

news.body:
How SEED renders a world players never stop building
Adam Axler - Unity
You can’t predict what players will build. In SEED, that’s the whole point – and the core rendering challenge.
SEED is Klang Games’s persistent MMO sandbox, built with Unity. It’s set on a distant planet where players manage autonomous characters called seedlings, build homes and businesses, trade in a player-driven economy, and organize societies with their own roles and laws. The world keeps running after players log off, and it’s continuously growing. Every new house, shop, tree, and seedling puts more pressure on Unity rendering performance, across hardware ranging from high-end PCs to phones.
The simulation itself runs on Klang Games’s servers. The Unity client’s job is to render whatever state the server streams in, so its workload depends on what players have built, not on what the team planned for.
“Since SEED is a fully server-authoritative game, the client mostly reads and renders the state and forwards player interactions, like clicking or camera movement,” says Artem Dyadichkin, graphics engineer at Klang Games.
We spoke with Dyadichkin and Nikita Fetisov, senior game engineer, about rendering player-built societies with the Universal Render Pipeline (URP), keeping thousands of small objects cheap, and using real player data to find bottlenecks on PC and mobile.
A world built from tiny pieces
SEED’s art style does a lot of the scaling work before any code runs. The game is stylized and low-poly, and instead of relying on textures, it stores most of its surface data in the geometry.
“Most of our color data is actually stored inside the vertex data,” says Dyadichkin. “The vertex data knows which color it is, which material definition it has – is it metal, is it smooth? All those things are baked into the meshes themselves.”
That saves on shading and memory bandwidth, which matters most on mobile.
Buildings take the same approach to an extreme. Instead of treating each structure as a single large mesh, SEED constructs buildings from many small, brick-like modules: walls, floors, roof edges, and corners on a one-meter grid. Players place coarse building blocks (voxels), and the game expands each one into around 15 modules, roughly half forming the building’s exterior and half its interior, which is generated only when a player looks inside. The largest society on one of SEED’s busiest islands has 172 buildings, made up of roughly 12,500 voxels, or 190,000 modules.
“We utilize BatchRendererGroup to render them and batch them together, and we do those batches through jobs,” says Dyadichkin. “Even though there are very many modules we need to render, buildings themselves have never really been a bottleneck in terms of pure rendering performance.”
Those jobs run on the C# Job System, and the team compiles them with the Burst compiler. Dyadichkin says they almost always go hand in hand in SEED’s client code.
Staying on the default path in URP
SEED uses URP to scale across PC and mobile, and Klang Games deliberately sticks close to Unity’s defaults.
“We try to stick to default solutions from Unity, so we can always be sure that whenever the next update comes, it gets covered,” says Dyadichkin.
That matters because the team upgrades Unity roughly once or twice a year – SEED currently runs on Unity 6.3 – picking up new rendering features as the project grows. Where the game needs something custom, the team extends URP rather than replacing it, using custom renderer features for game-specific effects and interactions.
Their use of Shader Graph follows the same principle. Nature assets use the default Lit shader, while characters and objects use Unlit shaders with a custom lighting pass. Either way, the team doesn’t have to worry about breaking URP’s performance features.
“You can be sure that if you create a shader graph, it won’t break SRP [Scriptable Render Pipeline] batching, and it won’t break GPU Resident Drawer,” Dyadichkin says. “Being certain that all the URP core features are still supported, while you still have space to customize whatever you want in a shader, is very powerful.”
That safety net matters in a world where players, not designers, decide how much the client has to draw.
Interacting with thousands of objects
The denser players build, the harder it gets to render a society – and to let them click on any part of it.
When players are zoomed in, SEED uses pixel-perfect picking. A custom renderer feature draws objects into a separate render target, an off-screen texture the GPU renders into instead of the screen. Each object is encoded with a unique ID that both the CPU and GPU can read. The client reads the pixel under the cursor to find exactly which object the player is hovering over.
On mobile, a fingertip is far less precise than a cursor, so the client also checks the pixels surrounding each tap. If it detects more than one object nearby, it shows the player a list to choose from, making smaller objects easier to select in densely built areas.
When players zoom out, the client switches back to physics raycasts, since GPU picking is harder to scale across a wide view.
Behind those raycasts sits a huge number of colliders. SEED uses Unity Physics not for simulation, but to bootstrap them quickly and query them.
“Every tree has a collider, every object and potentially every building brick can have one, and characters and seedlings do as well,” says Dyadichkin. “We can bootstrap this huge amount of colliders very quickly and then do queries against them for placement checks and other interactions.”
Once a player opens a building, its interior appears, and the client has more to track as they move between floors and inspect individual rooms. A continuously running job determines whether each object is inside or outside a building and which room and floor it occupies.
“That allows us to do all sorts of things – disable or enable GameObjects, or set the correct rendering layers to control the lighting situation,” Dyadichkin explains.
Profiling the world players actually built
The hardest part of optimizing for player-built worlds is getting realistic data. Klang Games gets it from the live game.
The team keeps server snapshots for disaster recovery, and once players have built large enough societies, those snapshots become test cases.
“We can restore what players have actually built and use that for performance testing and testing features at scale,” Fetisov says. “We can work with these built-out societies instead of starting from scratch or trying to simulate the data ourselves.”
Loading a snapshot of a large city locally exposed an unexpected CPU rendering bottleneck on PC.
“Our game is not GPU bottlenecked most of the time, but rather CPU bottlenecked,” says Dyadichkin. “It’s a very stylized, low-poly game with almost no textures.”
Using the Unity Profiler, Dyadichkin found the render thread spending more time than expected submitting draw calls. The team uses GPU Resident Drawer, so Dyadichkin expected it to instance those objects. The Frame Debugger showed otherwise.
“We were still defaulting to SRP batching rather than hybrid batching,” Dyadichkin says. “It turned out GPU Resident Drawer wasn’t capturing all these objects because almost all of our Prefabs have LOD Groups.”
The difference matters at SEED’s scale. The SRP Batcher reduces the CPU cost of setting up each draw call, but still submits one per object. GPU Resident Drawer goes further, grouping objects that share a mesh and material into instanced draws, which the Frame Debugger labels as hybrid batches. With thousands of small objects, that’s the difference between many lightweight draw calls and a few large ones.
The culprit behind the missed objects was animated LOD cross-fading. The effect looked better, but it kept the objects off the GPU Resident Drawer path.
“We disabled the animation portion. We still have cross-fading, but now with manually set transitions,” he says. “Now the draw calls are instanced again, which eased the load on our CPU render thread.”
Rendering a mature society within mobile memory
On mobile, SEED’s rendering hit a different constraint. “On the mobile side, we’re not CPU bound – we’re memory bound,” Fetisov says. “That is the main bane of our project.”
A mature society can contain enormous numbers of buildings, outdoor objects, characters, and meshes. Every mesh and material the client renders has to fit in memory first. Klang Games relies heavily on the Memory Profiler and memory snapshot comparisons to track down where that memory goes. The team found textures stored three times because of a broken reference, Addressables dependencies that duplicated the same material, and C# collections far larger than they needed to be.
“A lot came up where, on desktop, it was fine and people didn’t really notice it, but on mobile it was a big issue,” says Fetisov. “We relied on the Unity Memory Profiler quite a lot, especially [memory] snapshot diffs.”
Even without textures, geometry adds up.
“Some of the meshes were pretty chunky, especially the trees,” Fetisov says. “If you load all the LODs, a single tree can take megabytes of memory, and we have many tree variations.”
Because the team builds Addressables per platform, it can ship simplified trees to mobile without changing any game code. “The same code that loads the chair on desktop loads the chair on mobile,” Fetisov explains. “But the Addressables themselves can be assets optimized for mobile.”
The bigger shift was replacing LOD Groups on mobile altogether. Classic LODs meant storing multiple meshes per object type in memory – the same cost Fetisov describes with the trees. Mesh LOD, introduced in Unity 6.2, instead stores every level of detail inside a single mesh, and SEED’s mobile variants now use it exclusively. It also reduced the workload for Klang Games’s small art team.

members.title: 共赴新局！《金铲铲之战》发布2027电竞升级计划，PC版下赛季见

news.body:
11月6日，“金铲铲之战2027共赴新局：电竞升级·PC启航”发布会在西安御宴宫举行。适逢2026《金铲铲之战》公开赛秋季赛半决赛开战，《金铲铲之战》正式公布2027年电竞体系升级计划，并带来PC版的最新消息。
活动现场，腾讯游戏副总裁、腾讯互动娱乐《金铲铲之战》中国总负责人黄凌冬分享了产品及玩家生态发展成果，发布面向未来的赛事升级规划；腾讯互动娱乐《金铲铲之战》发行执行制作人叶菁介绍了专为电脑平台打造的《金铲铲之战》PC版。
以玩家热爱为起点，《金铲铲之战》将继续拓展策略竞技的参与方式，让更多弈士一起共赴新局。
携手2.4亿弈士同行，未来三年再投10亿
过去五年，《金铲铲之战》不断走进玩家日常。无论是随时随地开启一局对弈，还是与朋友分享阵容、复盘关键回合，策略竞技的乐趣已延伸到游戏内外。
发布会上，黄凌冬表示，上线五年来，《金铲铲之战》累计注册用户超2.4亿，月活跃用户突破5000万，全网话题播放量超2700亿次。仅今年9月，《金铲铲之战》相关内容全网每小时观看量便超过了1000万次。日益丰富的玩家交流与内容创作，让一局棋的精彩，有了更多被看见、被分享的方式。
为持续回应弈士们对产品内容、玩家文化与竞技体验的期待，立足已有生态积累，黄凌冬宣布《金铲铲之战》还将于未来三年再投入10亿元，用于玩家文化打造、内容创作者扶持和电竞赛事等生态建设领域，围绕产品、内容、社区与赛事持续加码，让不同类型的玩家都能找到属于自己的参与方式，也为策略竞技的长期发展积蓄力量。
七大升级开启“参与型电竞”新篇，千万总奖池铸就年度冠军赛殿堂
对于策略类游戏，竞技的精彩不仅在最终胜负，也在每一次选择与临场应变。《金铲铲之战》希望走出一条属于策略竞技的电竞之路：让高水平对弈被看见，也让更多普通玩家有机会亲自登上赛场。让每一份热爱都有机会走上舞台，是金铲铲探索策略类电竞的出发点。
围绕“参与型电竞”理念，团队持续完善办赛工具、赛事通道和专业解说体系，让参赛更便利，让比赛更好看，也让观众更容易理解选手的决策与博弈。发布会上，黄凌冬还公布了赛事参与数据：过去两年，《金铲铲之战》赛事参赛人次均超过1000万。
在此基础上，2027年电竞体系将迎来七大升级。首先，赛事体系将升级为“三大一超”架构，在全年三次全国公开赛（JOC）的基础上新增一届年度冠军赛。届时，来自不同赛事舞台的顶尖选手将在周年庆现场汇聚，角逐“冠军中的冠军”。与此同时，年度积分榜也将推出，链接全国公开赛、巅峰赛、平台赛、高校赛等多重渠道赛事表现，让选手的每一次参赛、每一份积累，都成为通向年度荣誉的重要一步。
与赛事体系同步升级的，是更具激励性的奖金设置。2027年，《金铲铲之战》电竞全年总奖金池将较2026年翻倍；年度冠军赛生态总奖池达到1000万元，其中年度冠军可获得总计300万元奖金。从公开赛的逐步进阶，到年度舞台的终极角逐，《金铲铲之战》将为每一位勇于挑战的弈士提供更明确的竞技目标。
观赛体验也将迎来焕新。全新八角舞台将让八位选手围坐一张棋桌同场对弈；专属粉丝区与多视角解说，则将帮助现场观众更深入地理解策略交锋背后的每一步博弈。
比赛之外，线下观赛体验将进一步升级为属于弈士们的棋友聚会：看比赛、见主播、与同好交流，或是随时坐下来“开铲”一局，让更多玩家既是赛场的见证者，也是这场聚会的参与者。
女子赛、高校赛焕新升级，一铲一城连接更多玩家
为让不同群体的热爱拥有专属舞台，《金铲铲之战》还将持续升级特色赛事。女子赛不仅引入顶流时尚品牌加持，为冠军时刻加冕，还通过与内容平台深度合作，为选手打造破圈内容。同时，还将定制专属游戏资产，为赛场上的她们留下独一无二的闪耀印记。
面向高校群体，《金铲铲之战》将推出全新高校赛事电竞品牌——“棱彩学院”，并针对这一专属于青年学子的电竞组织提供便捷办赛工具及百万级别生态激励，线下办赛规模也由原有的100场拓展至300场。赛事希望通过激励投入让比赛走进玩家身边，让更多热爱金铲铲的年轻人搭建属于自己的青春赛场。
从电竞舞台走向城市生活，《金铲铲之战》也将延续“落子中国，一铲一城”的探索。发布会上，黄凌冬对本次活动落地西安，特别感谢了西安市文旅局、曲江新区文旅局的指导和曲江文旅集团的支持。
未来，赛事计划还将走进成都、长沙、上海、深圳等城市，打造具有城市特色的赛事与玩家体验。让比赛成为相聚的理由，让不同城市的文化成为每一站独有的记忆，《金铲铲之战》期待与更多玩家在家门口见面。
PC版下个赛季见，端手互通开启更多“开铲”场景
赛事体系拉开新篇章的同时，叶菁还带来了《金铲铲之战》PC版的最新消息：“金铲铲之战PC版，将在接下来的，全新音乐主题赛季，与大家见面！”正式预约活动已于今日开启。
一直以来，玩家社区里都有希望在电脑上获得更好“开铲”体验的声音。为此，团队在延续移动端核心玩法与内容的基础上，推出专为电脑平台打造的PC版，以更具沉浸感的大屏视听和交互，将玩家熟悉的内容与对弈乐趣带进更多游玩场景。
视觉呈现上，PC版弈子战斗中的模型精度与贴图细节全面提升，融合PC独有渲染技术带来更细腻材质表现，高星级弈子的流动视觉效果，也让它们在棋盘上更有辨识度。竞技场则进行光源与环境调优，强化空间层次的同时更好地呈现棋盘细节。
操作上，PC版针对桌面端使用习惯优化界面布局与键鼠交互逻辑，并保留部分移动端操作习惯，让不同玩家都能找到顺手的操作方式。多端体验上，PC版将在账号数据、匹配机制及好友关系等方面，与移动端实现全方位互通，同时支持跨设备与好友同局竞技，实现真正的多端自由流转。
为迎接PC版，团队还将携手黄金品牌周大生定制一批“真金金铲铲挂坠”，将在PC版开测期间通过游戏内活动免费送出，弈士们只需参与即有机会赢取这份重磅好礼。
发布会现场还设置了PC版试玩区，媒体、内容创作者等嘉宾踊跃参与试玩，围绕PC版本体验展开交流。
携手点燃新局，西安决赛即将打响
发布会尾声，现场嘉宾共同登台，点燃“连胜之铲”，开启属于《金铲铲之战》的新赛年。这一仪式也体现了金铲铲以长期投入与多方协作持续建设玩家生态的决心。
新计划已经发布，新的冠军即将诞生。11月8日，2026《金铲铲之战》公开赛秋季赛全国总决赛将在西安打响。敬请期待弈士们在赛场上的精彩对弈，也期待与所有热爱金铲铲的玩家一起，在2027年共赴新局！

members.title: Mobile Game Gatekeepers Are Opening the Gates

news.body:
Mobile Game Gatekeepers Are Opening the Gates
For years, two companies decided which mobile games players ever saw. That is starting to change, and it changes what your next launch can look like.
I spend a lot of time thinking about a simple problem: there are more mobile games than ever, and it has never been harder for players to find the ones they will love. Top charts show the same handful of titles, and everything else is nearly invisible. If you shipped a mobile game recently, you already know the feeling.
This issue is why my co-founder Ivan Zenkovich and I started Skich back in 2020. It began as a small side project. We wanted to help players find games that actually fit them, not just the games with the biggest ad budgets. From the very first day, though, we had a bigger idea in mind. We wanted to build a real home for mobile players, one where they could discover a game and download it directly.
For a long time, the idea felt too new and a bit early. Two enormous stores controlled how games reached phones, leaving little room for anyone else. What changed my mind was watching the pressure build. Epic Games took on the gatekeepers in public. Antitrust regulators around the world started saying the same thing in their own way. It became clear that change was not a question of if but of when.
A rule change that finally opened the door
People often ask what Skich is. Some call it Tinder for mobile games, where you swipe and find your match. I prefer to think of it more like Spotify. Recommendations are only the start; we also give players game lists, a launcher, and social activity that works across platforms.
Skich runs on Android globally and on iOS in Europe. Until recently, that split came with a hard limit. The real challenge was never the technology. It was user acquisition. Getting someone to install a new store was unfamiliar, and on Android it felt a little risky.
Two things changed that in a matter of weeks. In early July, Apple lost its legal battle with the European Commission over the Digital Markets Act, which means we should see real change soon in how Apple follows the rules. Then, on July 22, Google Play in the United States opened its doors to alternative app stores. Players can now install them from Google Play with a single tap. Google Play also began sharing its full catalog with those stores.
That second change matters more than it might sound.
"For developers, this creates a zero-entry barrier. You can finally test whether there is real demand for your game outside the two big stores."
Discovery is Broken, and the Data Shows It
Mobile gaming has grown far past the roughly 20 genres the App Store recognizes. As AI makes games faster and cheaper to build, that number will climb, and the discovery problem climbs with it.
At Skich, we track more than 280 genres. Here is the part that surprised even us.
During onboarding, 70% of the genres that new players choose don't exist in traditional app stores.
Players already know what they like. The old stores just have no way to show it to them. That gap is the real opportunity, and it points to a part of the market almost everyone ignores.
I'm talking about the pre-release window. On our homepage, two sections draw the most interest: one is New This Week, where players find games that just launched. The other is Pre-releases, where players follow upcoming titles and sign up to hear the moment they go live. In the mid-core and hardcore space we focus on, players love this. They want to follow a game before launch, build anticipation, and feel part of the journey.
PC and console studios have understood this for years. They invest in brand building and pre-launch campaigns as a matter of course. Mobile has been slow to do the same, and I think that is a mistake worth fixing.
What a Developer Actually Gets
Matching the right player with the right game is the core of what we do. On top of that, we built tools meant to help a game spread on its own.
Two of them do most of the work. Game Lists let players collect and share the games they love. Activity shows a player's friends what they are doing, whether they start a game, write a review, add it to a wishlist, or drop it into a list. Every one of those actions becomes a small recommendation to someone who trusts them.
Then there are developer profiles; my favorite feature.
Half of the players who try one game from a developer go on to download another from that same studio through its Skich profile.
That is real brand awareness for developers, something the mobile market rarely offers.
A Fairer Deal on Money
The traditional store model has always bothered me on one point. You pay the same commission whether the store found your player or you did. That never felt fair.
So we do it differently. We charge a 15 percent commission only on the organic traffic we send you. If we did not help you find that player, we don't take a cut. We are also building a way for developers to bring their own audience into Skich, and we will share the terms for that once it is ready.
Who This is Really For
Right now, two groups are moving fastest toward alternative distribution. Large publishers want new channels they can own. Indie developers want organic traffic they cannot buy their way to. Mid-size studios are the most cautious so far, which I understand, though I suspect that will change as the path gets easier.
And it is getting easier. Distribution has always been our hardest problem, because installing a store through a website is strange behavior for most people, and Android's security warnings did not help. That is changing too. Alongside the US launch inside Google Play, Android has announced a simpler way to install alternative stores from websites worldwide. We have been getting ready for this moment for a while.
"Our website already brings in more than 100,000 new visitors every month, and that number keeps growing."
Where This Goes Next
I think we are about to see a market with dozens, maybe hundreds, of alternative stores, similar to what happened in China. The ones that last will not try to be everything to everyone. They will win by owning a specific niche and audience. For us, that means becoming the store mid-core and hardcore players trust, with games, developers, and features they cannot find anywhere else.
None of this works alone, though. Opening a new channel is one thing. Handling payments, taxes, and the operational work behind direct distribution is another, and it is not where most studios want to spend their energy.
This struggle is why we teamed up with Xsolla. We help developers step into direct distribution, while Xsolla handles the underlying payment processing and infrastructure. The goal was never to add more work to your plate. It was to give your game all the things it needs to reach players and grow, without asking you to rebuild your business to get there.
The gates are opening. For the first time in a long time, that is genuinely good news for the people who make games.
Sergey Budkovski, Co-Founder and CEO of Skich
A pioneer of alternative mobile game distribution. He is building a next-generation mobile game store, with personalized discovery and social features for players and better economics for game developers.

news.title: This Forgotten Classic D&D RPG Was Revived Without Source Code or Tools
news.summary_raw: SNEG had no source code, tools, or documentation for this 2001 PC RPG, forcing the team to reverse-engineer the game from its retail releases when building out its modern remaster.

members.title: This Forgotten Classic D&D RPG Was Revived Without Source Code or Tools

news.body:
This Forgotten Classic D&D RPG Was Revived Without Source Code or Tools
SNEG had no source code, tools, or documentation for this 2001 PC RPG, forcing the team to reverse-engineer the game from its retail releases when building out its modern remaster.
In case you missed it
More Game Details
After nearly 25 years of limited availability, the long-lost D&D RPG Pool of Radiance: Ruins of Myth Drannor is now available on Steam and GOG. The restoration brings Stormfront Studios’ divisive but ambitious Dungeons & Dragons RPG to modern PCs with widescreen support up to 4K, controller compatibility, a reworked camera, a faster interface, numerous bug fixes, and an optional Legacy mode.
Actually recovering the game was considerably more complicated than updating a few assets. SNEG had no original source code, development tools, or documentation. Its team began with the international retail editions and whatever remained on those discs, eventually reverse-engineering enough of the game to modify its original engine. Dear ImGui became the foundation for the new interface, while AMD FSR 1.0 helped produce sharper output without altering the original artwork.
In the following interview, SNEG Co-Founder Artem Shchuiko explains why the studio believed a game with such a troubled reputation deserved another opportunity. Check out the game for yourself if you want to see more.
Pool of Radiance: Ruins of Myth Drannor
Pool of Radiance: Ruins of Myth Drannor originally launched in 2001 and has been difficult to access on modern systems for years. What made this particular Dungeons & Dragons title worth restoring, and what were the first steps in bringing it back?
Artem Shchuiko: The game has a bad reputation. But if you look past its weak points, what you find is a flawed yet thoroughly enjoyable RPG that never reached enough players and clearly suffered from a compressed development cycle. It’s also the latest entry in the Phlan saga, and it was the first video game to implement what was then the brand-new D&D ruleset. And there’s another angle that makes this one special: it was a homecoming to D&D for Don Daglow and his team, a decade after their Gold Box and Neverwinter Nights days, not to mention it being Stormfront’s last RPG.
Restoring a game that is nearly 25 years old can present some unusual technical challenges. What original source code, development tools, documentation, and assets were available to the team, and how did their condition affect the restoration process?
Artem Shchuiko: None of it, unfortunately. No source code, no tools, no documentation. The only thing we had to work from was the retail editions released around the world and whatever was on those discs. That obviously shaped our starting point and limited how much we could change, especially early on.
The re-release supports widescreen resolutions up to 4K and features upscaled background assets. Can you walk us through the visual restoration pipeline, including how you approached upscaling original artwork, maintaining visual consistency, and preserving the atmosphere of the 2001 release?
Artem Shchuiko: First, a correction: the re-release doesn’t feature upscaled background or terrain assets. That’s something we’re exploring for later.
Our overall approach was simple: whatever we touch or introduce has to stay true to the legacy look. Take the Action Bar. It’s a new UI element, and it also meant creating icons for every spell and action in the game. We could easily have made them look modern, but that would be out of touch with the rest of the game. At the same time, we didn’t want to draw them at the original low resolution either. So we settled on a rule for these new assets: 2x the original. That gives enough pixels to not look bad while keeping the dated look and feel, as a feature. It’s easy nowadays to just scale everything up, but that breaks the immersion, and we didn’t want that.
The one exception was the game’s main font. That’s the one thing we knew had to be as crisp as possible. We reconstructed the original font as a proper TTF and added the missing glyphs, which gave us the best readability we could get without losing the original character.
The game includes a reworked camera, improved UI, new action bar, and additional tooltips. How did you approach redesigning these elements for modern displays and controls while retaining the look and feel of a classic Dungeons & Dragons CRPG?
Artem Shchuiko: Our top priorities were the actual moment-to-moment gameplay: fixes, the information you’re given to make decisions, and the pace of the game, which suffers a lot in the 2001 edition. We also had to balance that against what players are used to today, so we were careful not to go against established modern conventions. But largely, step one was listing every action and pattern in the game that either takes too many unnecessary steps or doesn’t show you enough to make a decision.
Retaining the original look and feel was actually the easy part. We decided early on that the visuals would only get a minor boost, because reworking them properly means redrawing from scratch, and that’s remake territory from how we see it. Our goal was never to remake the game. We wanted to re-release it properly this time - keep what made the original special, but make it much easier for people to actually play it today.
The original game was designed for mouse-and-keyboard PC gameplay, but the restoration introduces full controller support and Steam Deck compatibility. What were the biggest design and engineering challenges involved in adapting its interface, navigation, party management, and turn-based combat for those devices?
Artem Shchuiko: Controller support is simply expected today, so on this project it couldn’t be ignored. We didn’t want the UI to stray too far from the original, but that UI was never designed with a controller in mind. On top of that, it was essentially a hardcoded set of images, because back then there were no off-the-shelf UI engines to build on.
That line of thinking quickly led us to an action bar. It was the single most valuable UI improvement for the game: it works equally well with either input method, and it also solved a number of pacing issues. Once it was in, along with new icons for skills and spells, we started testing layouts situation by situation and iterated as much as we could. Combat early in the game and near the end, inventory management, moving around outside combat: every one of these interactions went through multiple passes, and each pass gave us a clearer sense of what works and what doesn’t.
For abstract questions like “what feels right” or “what would a player expect,” we relied on our own experience as players. We challenged each other internally, ran every major milestone past external QA, and finally put the game in front of players as a demo. That gave us a reality check from outside our own bubble.
The Steam Deck, and the handheld experience in general, was at the core of development from the start. The whole project was tested on it first. I’d be lying if I said the experience is flawless, but I personally prefer playing Pool of Radiance Ruins of Myth Drannor on a handheld.
How did you approach making changes to the original game's systems without unintentionally affecting combat balance, pacing, or the rules that define the experience?
Artem Shchuiko: That’s a good question. Normally I’d worry about a lot more, but with Pool of Radiance: Ruins of Myth Drannor the problems were vivid and right in your face, so the scope of critical changes was clear from the start. The open question was how far to go, and that’s where iteration helped us regulate ourselves on what to touch and what to leave alone.
For example, we could easily have drifted toward letting players choose their feats, adding missing classes like the mage, or nerfing the pre-made characters, which have more points than the default character creation allows. All of these are reasonable expectations. But we quickly realised that touching them without going further would actually make things worse. Suddenly we’d be working on a remaster, which by nature intrudes on the systems, where one change inevitably demands the next. In that paradigm, the old UI has to be thrown away and rebuilt. Add redrawn graphics and a move to the latest D&D ruleset, and you’re already looking at a remake of sorts.
So we very consciously, to our own regret as gamers, set a rule: no changes to the core game systems unless something is clearly a bug. That rule became our guiding principle for this re-release.
What software, engines, tools, or custom technologies did the team use throughout the restoration process? Were there any particularly difficult problems involving compatibility, rendering, animation, asset formats, or other legacy systems that required creative technical solutions?
Artem Shchuiko: After a substantial reverse-engineering effort, we decided to stay on the original engine and make our changes inside the legacy build. Part of the reason was speed, and part was staying true to the game’s look and feel. With that as our foundation, we tried replacing the UI with various modern frameworks, but quickly realised that Dear ImGui, of all things, let us iterate fastest on this particular game. The hardest part wasn’t the UI itself. It was building an internal API to expose the data the new UI needed, much of which was buried deep inside the original code.
For image sharpness, we built on a process we’d already established on other titles, using AMD’s FSR 1.0 to deliver sharper visuals without modifying the original assets. Stability and low system requirements matter a lot to us, so we also use several of our own in-house libraries to stay compatible with the widest possible range of hardware without inflating resource usage.
Classic CRPGs have experienced renewed interest in recent years, particularly following the success of modern Dungeons & Dragons games.

members.title: Elections signal cultural shifts that no creative industry can dare to ignore | Opinion

news.body:
Elections signal cultural shifts that no creative industry can dare to ignore | Opinion
The games industry has kowtowed to the cultural logic of conservative ascendancy for years – this week's US election shows how out of touch with the broader audience that has been
There is a perfectly logical way in which you can look at an election result – even a truly seismic election result – and say that it is largely irrelevant to the business decision-making of the games industry. Elections do not change your customer demographics; all of Washington or Westminster or Nagatachō may change overnight, but the people who bought your games yesterday are still the people who will buy them tomorrow, aren't they?
If you follow that logic… well, nothing has really changed. The world of politics may have shifted, but that doesn't change the facts on the ground. If yesterday decisions were made that the best way to engage and satisfy your audience was to pull back from diversity and minimise representation, then those decisions must make an equal amount of sense today. It's not like the audience changed.
Yet you knew that was wrong, even as you read it. Democracy at scale is still a new and surprisingly thinly understood thing, but we all have a pretty strong sense that elections shift more than just the bums on seats in a legislative chamber. Elections move culture. They embolden, or cow, whole swathes of the public; they crown cultural ascendants and kick the legs out from under former icons whose moment is now past.
The overall climate around tech regulation is likely to shift to a stricter stance
That function of shifting the cultural moment could not be more relevant to an industry like the games business. Video games sit at the intersection of the technology and media industries, two areas which have been deeply embroiled in the tug-of-war that's played out over the soul of America and of the wider world in recent years. The fortunes of both of those will be changed significantly by the political and cultural changes set in motion by this week's US elections. Nearly every part of the video games industry will in turn be touched, at least to some degree, by those changes.
Some changes will be very overt. The incoming crop of Democratic Party legislators at both state and national level seem, on the whole, to be chomping at the bit about regulating tech industries, and are likely to overturn many aspects of the extremely laissez-faire regulatory environment that has prevailed for the past few years (including, to a certain degree, under the Biden administration).
Much of their early focus is likely to be on data centres – and ten states passed ballot measures against data centre construction as well, demonstrating voter appetite for such restrictions – but the overall climate around tech regulation is likely to shift to a stricter stance in many regards. It's unlikely the United States will get as keen on tech regulation as the European Union, whose scepticism about the international influence of US tech giants and their billionaire owners continues to grow month to month. But equally, the way that so many of those billionaire owners threw themselves into full-throated support for, and full-walleted obsequence to, far-right movements over the past two years has likely made them quite an array of implacable foes who now occupy positions of significant legislative power.
The gut reaction of many people in the games business will probably be to clutch their pearls at the notion of such regulation – a lot of senior people in this business really do consider themselves to be temporarily embarrassed tech billionaires, after all (a solid chunk of the remainder consider themselves to be temporarily embarrassed Hollywood moguls). The actual effects, however, are likely to be mixed, and perhaps more favourable than not.
Certainly, some of the regulatory efforts we're likely to see in the coming years will also slap the knuckles of the games business, albeit only in passing. Federal regulations on online gambling will largely aim at grotesque businesses like Kalshi and Polymarket, but may well catch some loot box and gacha mechanisms in the blast radius if they're actually enacted. So it goes; it was only a matter of time before a major market gutted those questionable business models anyway. Child protection laws targeting social media companies may well, if enacted, catch the likes of Roblox in the noose as well. That's also been predicted for some time – the election results merely make it more likely to actually happen in the foreseeable future.
The real prize is the possibility that this election is a sharp enough pin pressed against the straining membrane of the AI bubble to actually precipitate a pop
Other effects, however, would turn out far more favourable for games businesses. A renewed focus on aspects like net neutrality and a general environment of more sceptical regulation of giant-scale platform holders will generally favour companies trying to sell games and services across these platforms and networks.
Needless to say, though, the real prize on offer here is the possibility that this election is a sharp enough pin pressed against the straining membrane of the AI bubble to actually precipitate a pop – or at least a rapid deflation. There are games companies that are bullish on the prospects of AI in various aspects, for sure, but even the most bullish of them would probably gleefully cancel all their Claude subscriptions tomorrow if it got GPUs and consoles back to reasonable consumer prices overnight. Between the anti-data-centre ballot initiatives and the vastly more AI-sceptical incoming legislatures, the environment in the United States is going to become a lot more hostile to the bubble's continued expansion; it won't fix the component crisis overnight and a hell of a lot of financial pain will occur along the way, but perhaps there's now a dim light at the end of the tunnel.
It's also worth noting that the deflation of the AI bubble should also knock a bit of sanity back into the games industry's finances, which have been brutalised in recent years by a gigantic shift in investor interest towards AI projects. Again, it won't be fast – there'll be a lot of wounds to be licked for a while – but once the AI blinkers come off, eventually investors looking for an interesting tech-adjacent sector to make some bets in should start glancing back in this direction.
That's a lot of ifs and buts, of course; we're making big assumptions about the willingness of America's new politicians and institutions to really take on the tech industry, and of course, that industry will have its own agency and its own desire to keep the bubble going as long as possible. What's rather more certain, though, goes right back to what I said at the start; it's hard to tell what the political shift will deliver, but the cultural shift already looks stone-cold certain.
In part, it's about who feels emboldened. Their voices get louder and their certainty that they speak for a majority gets unshakeable. An election that sweeps the legs from underneath their movement is humbling to a degree that no simple poll ever seems like it should be; when your worldview has rested on the notion that you speak for a gigantic, invisible majority who all think exactly like you, the discovery that you're doing nothing of the sort can be devastating, isolating, and silencing. Not necessarily a bad thing; if what you've used that misbegotten confidence to promote is hatred and bigotry, that silence will be hard-won bliss for everyone else.
It's been obvious forever that you win over far bigger audiences through better representation than you lose
Not that I think we can expect silence. The people who have railed for years against diversity, against minorities, against every kind of representation or nuance or even basic compassion appearing in video games – they'll still be around and they'll still be noisy. What is changed is that we now see how small and narrow the slice of the market they spoke for actually is. Absolutely nobody can claim with any degree of credibility that they represent anything other than what they seem; not the inevitable future of culture, but an angry, slightly pitiful, and almost entirely commercially irrelevant sub-sub-grouping.
This isn't some grand revelation. Lots of people have known for years that the only way for the games industry to grow out of its moribund audience size is to diversify and expand, exploring new themes and ideas, winning over new audiences. It's been obvious forever that you win over far bigger audiences through better representation than you lose; that the handful of vociferously angry people whose imagination cannot stretch to identifying with anyone other than a burly grunting white man will never make a whit of difference to your bottom line.
Yet for all that those things have been clear, there have still been so many decisions made in fear, and in a kind of cowardice dressed up as caution, in recent years. Much of it's probably down to how many people in the industry still choose to sit in echoing chambers of Twitter's corpse, hot-boxing themselves with the world's angriest compulsive masturbators, its richest white supremacist, and an untold number of half-demented bots until the fumes tell them that this is somehow representative of their actual audience. Perhaps that can be the first step of your adjustment to the new cultural reality we're waking up to; recognise that you've been fooling yourself, and allowing yourself to be fooled, about the relevance of X, and get the hell off that site. If the industry wants to position itself for what's next, disentangling itself from the architects of what's dead and dying has to be step one.

news.title: Sony insists its next-generation console plans are still on schedule
news.summary_raw: As part of the media giant's quarterly financial report, Sony states that progress toward the next generation of consoles is proceeding on schedule.

members.title: Sony insists its next-generation console plans are still on schedule

news.body:
In Sony's Q2 financial report, the company announced that it's lifting its full-year profit forecast by 9 percent, 2.6 million PlayStation 5 units were sold this past quarter, and that it does not fear the ongoing memory crisis. Sony is, in fact, moving ahead with plans for next-generation hardware in the next fiscal year with confidence.
"Looking ahead to next fiscal year, we aim to continue to enhance user engagement and further strengthen monetization through the release of strong titles and the expansion of our service," the financial report reads. "We also intend to make solid progress in preparing for the next generation platform."
Later in the Q&A, which you can review here, one investor asked Sony CFO Lin Tao if the company's next-generation hardware plans were still on schedule.
"So this is a next-generation R&D," Tao answered. "We are progressing as scheduled. So for the next-generation investment, so the second half would be a large impact of the investment amount. And the development itself is on schedule."
Another investor from BofA Securities asked how Sony is dealing with the rise in memory prices and the effect that will have on profitability going into a new generation. Tao also fields this question, stating that they have to assume that their production pipeline will be capable enough to produce units, with executive officer Naoya Horii chiming in that Sony has a deal with TMSC to assuage concerns of supply limitations.
The PlayStation 5 itself has reached a 97.9 million units shipped milestone, a virtual guarantee to cross the 100 million units threshold in the coming quarter. Marvel's Wolverine sold 2.4 million copies in the two months since release, which puts it in dire straits when directly compared to games like Marvel's Spider-Man 2, which Sony reported as selling 2.5 million copies on its first day of release. A more recent comparison, Ghost of Yotei, sold 3.3 million copies in its first month, also according to Sony.
Mutant superheroes aside, the quarterly results paint a rosy picture for PlayStation, but the looming discussion of price for the next generation of hardware hangs over any excitement over upcoming plans. While Sony seems confident that the memory crisis won't affect next-generation ambitions, it is difficult to see how that can truly be the case when you consider Sony CEO Hiroki Totoki expressing skepticism for just that reason a few months ago.

news.title: Jobs roundup: November | Nordisk Games appoints Stefanía Halldórsdóttir as CEO and Ásgeir Kröyer as CFO
news.summary_raw: It can be difficult keeping track of the various comings and goings in the games industry, which is why we compile them in semi-regular round-ups.

members.title: Jobs roundup: November | Nordisk Games appoints Stefanía Halldórsdóttir as CEO and Ásgeir Kröyer as CFO

news.body:
Jobs roundup: November | Nordisk Games appoints Stefanía Halldórsdóttir as CEO and Ásgeir Kröyer as CFO
Gamescom Dev organiser Game Events GmbH names Sasha Volkohon head of commercial
It can be difficult keeping track of the various comings and goings in the games industry, which is why we compile them in semi-regular round-ups.
If you have new appointments or transitions in your company that belong here, please send the names of appointees, new role and company, and prior role and company to newhires@gamesindustry.biz.
Nordisk Games appoints Stefanía Halldórsdóttir as CEO and Ásgeir Kröyer as CFO
Nordisk Games has named Stefanía Halldórsdóttir as CEO and Ásgeir Kröyer as CFO.
These appointments follow the recent publishing agreement between subsidiaries Avalanche Studios Group and Supermassive Games.
Halldórsdóttir and Kröyer will retain their positions as CEO and CFO of Avalanche Studios Group.
"Stefanía and Ásgeir have built Avalanche Studios Group into everything we want our studios to be: creatively ambitious, operationally excellent and growing," said former interim CEO and Nordisk Film chair Allan Mathson Hansen.
"Putting that experience at the centre of Nordisk Games is the natural next step for the group. With this new leadership in place, we look forward to continuing to pursue our growth ambitions within games."
Halldórsdóttir added: "I'm proud to take this on, and grateful to Allan for the foundation he's laid and the trust he's shown. Nordisk Games should be an active owner that gives its studios what they need to do their best work."
"For us, that starts with investing in games and the teams behind them. Our studios lead their games creatively, and everything we do as an owner is in service of that work; that's the reason this group works. Ásgeir and I will continue to lead from Stockholm, which remains home for us."
Sasha Volkohon | Head of commercial, Game Events GmbH
Game Events GmbH, organiser of Gamescom Dev, has appointed Sasha Volkohon as head of commercial, succeeding Roufina Guenkova.
Volkohon was previously senior business development manager at Remote Control Productions.
As head of commercial, Volkohon will oversee the firm's event portfolio, including Gamescom Dev and its leadership events.
"We are excited to welcome Sasha as our new head of commercial," said Game Events GmbH managing director Frederik Hammes. "Her experience working with developers, publishers, and other industry partners at Remote Control Productions is particularly relevant to our events."
"Together, we want to strengthen existing partnerships and develop new commercial opportunities across Gamescom Dev, our year-round leadership events, and the wider event portfolio."
Three former Warhorse Studios devs join CD Projekt Red
As spotted by GamesRadar, three developers from Warhorse Studios have joined CD Projekt Red to work on The Witcher 4.
Karel Kolmann is now senior quest designer at CD Projekt Red, after serving as lead gameplay designer at Warhorse.
Zdeněk Glatz is senior open world designer following his role at Warhorse as lead level designer, and Zbyněk Zelinka has been appointed senior gameplay designer, following his tenure as lead technical designer at Warhorse.
Stewart Neal | Partnerships & growth director, Mandali Games
Stewart Neal has been appointed partnerships & growth director at Mandali Games. Neal previously served as studio director at Sumo India Studios.
Neal joined Sumo Digital in 2014 and held roles as insource/outsource manager, development manager, and external content director until 2020.
"Mandali has a rich heritage, a strong foundation and a talented team with experience working on some fantastic games," said Neal. I'm genuinely excited to join Priyam Dutta and the team, and build on what they've achieved and help shape Mandali's next chapter."

news.body:
Sega Q2 results exceed expectations, driven by surge in operating income for pachislot and pachinko machines
Entertainment Contents segment revenue, which includes games, fell 2.4% to $916.8 million
Sega's second quarter results for 2026 have exceeded expectations, driven by a 331.6% surge in operating income for its pachislot and pachinko machines business.
The firm also noted its Entertainment Contents segment exceeded expectations, despite revenue dropping 2.4% to ¥145.1 billion ($916.8 million).
The Numbers
For the three months ended September 30, 2026
- Net sales: ¥212.5 billion ($1.3 billion), up 5.6% year-on-year
- Entertainment Contents net sales (including games): ¥145.1 billion ($916.8 million), down 2.4%
- Operating income: ¥14.2 billion ($89.7 million), up 42% year-on-year
The highlights
Sega reported a 23.5% decline in full game sales to ¥20.5 billion ($129.5 million), down from ¥26.8 billion ($169.3 million) in the same period last year. 10.6 million full game units were sold during the quarter, up from 9.3 million year-on-year.
New titles generated ¥0.3 billion ($1.8 million) in revenue, down from ¥8.7 billion ($54.9 million). Catalogue sales reached ¥20.2 billion ($127.6 million), a 12.2% increase from ¥18 billion ($113.7 million).
Free-to-play sales "performed slightly below expectations," falling 3.3% to ¥26.0 billion ($164.3 million).
DLC and subscription services "performed steadily," and Rovio "performed generally in line with expectations."
Earlier this year, GamesIndustry.biz spoke to Angry Birds creative officer Ben Mattes about life under Sega following its $776 million acquisition in 2023 and the subsequent $200 million impairment.
"They know that we're a transmedia company. They know that we're a mobile-first company. They know that they've had successes with Sonic. They know that they want to grow their mobile expertise," said Mattes.
"So of course from day zero, the ambition has been to make Angry Birds every bit as big as Sonic is from a transmedia point of view, and grow not just the Rovio mobile free-to-play business, but all of Sega's mobile and free-to-play expertise and live-ops expertise across its portfolio."
Looking ahead, Sega expects "expansion in new title and catalogue sales" through sales transformation initiatives, as well as increased licensing revenue from its transmedia rollout.
Sega also noted wishlist trends for upcoming titles Stranger Than Heaven and Persona 4 Revival.
For Stranger Than Heaven, launching in January 2027, wishlists have exceeded one million, "outperforming benchmark titles at the same stage before release." Additionally, "new users account for approximately half of wishlist registrations."
Wishlists for Persona 4 Revival, releasing in February 2027, exceeded two million and is likewise outperforming benchmark titles. The report noted that "a high proportion of registrants have purchased multiple titles in the series."

members.title: 在AI战争中幸存的策划

news.body:
“先活下来会比较重要。”
2025年的某天，潇潇所在的项目突然被内部评估为“赛道前景不大”，随后被取消。那是某个大厂的搜打撤项目，已经开发接近2年，潇潇在项目里担任系统及关卡负责人。项目被取消后，他需要寻找能够接纳他的新项目。
一开始，潇潇只是感到有些可惜，但觉得影响不大。毕竟当时市场上的搜打撤赛道正火热。可他没想到，当他准备寻找新项目时，不论是公司内还是其他外部厂商，都不再对他的履历感兴趣了。
“项目取消之后，我去看过公司内部‘活水’（内部调岗）机会，符合的岗位很少，我也去问过几次，但聊完之后都没有反馈了。”潇潇说。
潇潇今年已经四十多岁，在2005年入行。入行时进的第一个项目是《仙剑奇侠传四》，他担任文案策划。后来他陆续进过腾讯、网易等大厂，历任关卡策划、数值策划、组长、系统负责人，最高做过主策划和项目主创。从业经历称得上丰富，此前，他的项目履历几乎未曾有过空档。
但现在，潇潇发现，自己的履历似乎“没有用了”。适合他的岗位都在二次元和开放世界项目里，但他年纪太大了，“一般这种项目都会直接认为老策划不懂年轻玩家，不予考虑。而且我还比别人贵”。最好的一次，潇潇面到了某个公司的副总，但最后还是没有下文。
几次面试碰壁后，一位HR告诉潇潇，像他这样的情况，现在要走“公司特批”才能进去——原因在于，虽然他有着很丰富的项目履历，但在当下的职场里，这些积累下来的能力和经验，不再像以往一样有着高估值。而他也算不上明星策划，没办法为项目带来额外的影响力。
潇潇意识到，他的职业困境在于：以他的资历，如果只是进入一个小项目，从职业追求的角度来看意义不大。但如果想要进入大项目，从目前的市场情况来看，很难获得机会。
“我是土木工程毕业的，当年毕业的时候正好赶上了房地产起来的那几年，但我就是想做游戏，所以才一头扎进了游戏圈里。那时候做游戏一个月才1500元。”潇潇对我说，他总结，以往策划的职业生涯还有机会走到50岁，但如今这个年龄关或许将要被提前到35岁以前。
表面上的原因有很多：项目年轻化、职场竞争、降本增效……总体来说，这些因素在过去一直存在，尽管此前行业同样艰难，他并未想到自己会因此失业。但现在，新的变量出现了。
“我觉得导致‘年龄关’被提前的最大变量还是AI，”潇潇说，“我发现，我们这种老策划的经验，慢慢地在AI面前变得不那么重要了。现在我们和AI之间，就好像在打一场无形的战争。”
这场“战争”来得非常迅猛，以至于很多和潇潇一样的“老策划”还没反应过来，他就无可避免地从原有的位置上滑落了。在过去，他们最大的优势在于经验、决策和判断，但现在，AI改变了团队讨论和判断设计的方式，老策划的话语权也因此开始松动。他们渐渐感到，自己的经验不再像过去那样被需要。
在潇潇的感受里，变化从2025年年初开始。起初，AI带来的变化非常细微，大家都只是把它当作一个可以让自己更快完成工作的小帮手。之后，随着AI能力不断升级，潇潇所在的团队将AI接入了工作流中。
公司原本有一套项目管理系统，包括策划、美术、程序等板块在内的所有内容都会通过这个系统由PM（项目经理）统一管理。AI被接入到这套系统里，项目的推进流程也随之发生改变。
“比如说，你是项目经理，要做一个游戏，你可以用AI一键生成PM的需求单，它会拆分好各个板块需要完成的任务，自动地把项目成员作为处理人放进去，然后把需求对应发出去。”潇潇说。
他继续补充：“收到了项目需求的策划会发现系统里也有一个AI功能的按钮，按下去可以帮你把技术文档写完，然后文档流转到下一个流程，据我所知，比如技术评审、开发也是有个类似的AI评审功能，他们也会把任务交给AI去做……”
最后，开发完的内容会给测试进行QA。“不过测试还是由人负责的，”潇潇说，“因为目前这个由AI来做的话成本更高。”
与此同时，随着AI能力的不断提升，团队习惯使用AI来辅助输出方案的同时，潇潇觉得自己团队里老策划的权威也在被一点点消磨。
在过去，一个项目中，资深策划往往在自己负责的板块里拥有绝对的权威。这种权威展现在或大或小的方面，最明显的时候可能是工作群里几句话的讨论：当有其他策划提出不同的想法时，负责相关板块的老策划往往可以凭借地位和经验优势压制对方——甚至可以说，几乎没有人敢表现出不同的想法，“这本身就已经是非常越界的行为了”。
“在AI之前，负责某个玩法板块的owner只要出了设计，一般都会被通过，群里会适时出现一片赞美，最多是会有人提些不痛不痒的交互建议。”但在AI出现之后，情况发生了变化，开始有一些新人开始尝试用AI来挑战老策划的权威。比如，拿着AI推导过的结果来“争论”。
这种争论并没有到激烈的程度，大部分情况下，老策划还是可以轻易地反驳回去。但氛围已经发生了变化：对很多老策划来说，很多工作的推进是事前已经明确的分工，大家都习惯了在工作时“自扫门前雪”；而且，如果每个成熟的设计都需要再做一次讨论，对项目推进来说也是无用功。更何况，出于效率和稳定性考量，老策划常常需要交出一些相对保守的设计。
但对于亟需展示自己能力的新人来说，这些行为是难以理解的，甚至令他们“不齿”的。潇潇感觉，在过去，新人缺乏经验，也缺乏时间和精力去人工验证一个理论的正确性；而AI强大的分析、推导能力成为了如今新人展示自己想法的有力武器。
潇潇举了一个例子，之前，他在某个射击游戏里亲自设计和落地了一个“局内标识队友位置”的罗盘逻辑，在后来的另外一个项目中，也需要制作一个一样的功能。这个功能被交给一位新人负责，新人很自然地就使用了AI做反推设计，最终成品和潇潇初始的设计有所出入，但仍被投入使用。
“基于AI的设计能力，它成了新人的第二个权威来源。让他们又看到了弯道超车的机会。”潇潇说，“打个比方，本来新人60分，老人90分，AI相当于给新人都加了20分，他们就有机会了。”
变化不仅发生在新老之间，很多新人之间的争论也开始更大幅度地涉及到AI。过去，新人策划间的争论一般由老策划来调停，他们会以自身经验来判断谁的设计更加正确，但很多时候，这种经验主义也让他们难以清楚地解释具体原因。而现在，AI似乎成为了一个更加“公正”的裁决者。
“很多老策划可能也讲不清楚原因，只是知道都是这样做的。”潇潇说。但正是这种模糊，让新人在接触老策划时加强了不信任感。他们转投向AI，可在潇潇看来，AI才是那个“平等地偏爱双方的角色”。
“我遇到过的情况是，新人策划如果问AI一些开放式的问题，比如‘我这样设计好吗’，AI就会告诉他‘我觉得这样设计很好’。这时候，如果其他人不认同这个方案，这个策划就会说‘你去我工位看看我的AI是怎么说的’，看完之后，反对者又会拿自己的意见去问自己的AI，AI又会为他输出一版有利于他的结论。两边就这样用AI互相反驳了起来，没完没了。”潇潇说。
另一方面，在团队之外，潇潇担心，随着AI深度参与游戏开发，未来的游戏项目留给策划施展想法的空间会变小。换句话说，如果策划这个岗位本身的价值都在受到AI挑战，新人是否有“话语权”，或许也将失去意义。
潇潇说：“当年我曾经还参加过某个IP改编项目。当时，围绕是否要显示伤害数字，策划们吵得很厉害。有的策划觉得不显示数字才能还原原作的真实感，有的策划则认为只有数字才能体现出玩家的成长变化。那时候大家都是新人，每个人都会尽可能地表达自己的想法。但现在很少了，意义也不大。一般到最后，都是要看上面的意思。”
AI Agent出现之后，潇潇发现行业使用AI的趋势更进一步。他接触过的一些团队已经不满足于将AI用作辅助完成任务的工具，它们的架构也因AI发生偏移。
潇潇最直观的感受，是项目的推进变得更“规范”了。
他以某个“搜打撤”游戏的设计为例。以往，老策划的界面布局往往会照搬模板设计，美术人员也习惯于接受这种需求。他解释道：“因为这不是核心的验证点，对于美术人员来说做起来也更容易。”但“老板”就会问AI：有没有更好的优化方案——在这些场景下，AI会做很多为了优化而优化、为了差异而差异的事情，导致潇潇之前的团队里，原来相对轻松的工作都要重新做一遍。潇潇认为：“有人说AI来了之后，大厂的‘人效比’没有上去，我觉得这也是一个因素。”
在过去，大多数游戏产品开发会由一个主策划把控整体的需求和产出。主策划最直接的价值体现在过往的项目经验上，一个优秀的策划可以把此前开发过程中积累的经验和教训内化成某种“感觉”，将其打磨为自己的设计理念或标准，并应用在之后项目的所有生产管线中。而现在，这种“标准”也在被挑战。
潇潇也是一样，之前他曾负责过某个搜打撤项目的系统组。在设计游戏中的物品尺寸时，团队里的“老策划”会希望按照传统搜打撤类产品的方法，完全按照写实的物体尺寸比例去做背包的格子数量——大的东西占的格子多，小的东西格子少。而新策划则会觉得，“这并不重要。”
“就是沿着‘IRL（In Real Life）准则’走的，”他说，“老一点的策划会觉得有些东西就是准绳，你不能越过。而新人觉得不重要，有很大一部分原因也是因为他们有这些AI工具的结论支持：AI会说，理论上，游戏趣味性比拟真之类的规范可能更重要。这看起来比老策划的‘准绳’更有说服力。”
与此同时，当AI的产出能力越来越稳定之后，AI生成的策划案往往在内容上更全面，呈现也更美观，老策划用经验写下的设计似乎就显得比较“粗糙”，给人更加不可靠的感受。
主策划本人的表达也有可能影响项目，并不是所有人都能清晰、平和地表达自己的想法，而AI可以做到。而且，大家越来越开始担心单人的主策划不如AI那样全面——潇潇观察到，如果一个项目的主策划是某个功能性岗位出身，比如数值、美术，那高层总是会担心游戏在研发过程中被带偏，“如果‘主策’出现脑子不清楚的情况，那项目或许就完了。”
“现在，有些我知道的大厂已经不喜欢由‘主策’来主导所有模块了。甚至，你去看一些大厂公开的团队名单，会发现他们已经没有标出具体的‘主策’岗位了。”他说。
没有主策之后，项目就变成了“谁出钱谁负责”。潇潇说：“实际的项目负责人会变成内部的某个‘老板’，可以理解为类似‘投资人’的角色，他负责整个项目的投入产出。要立项时，‘老板’首先会拉起一批核心的成员，一起做个demo，然后内部评审。如果评审结果不错，就结合反馈意见再调整调整……两三次之后，如果demo达到要求，就可以开始立项、招人。”
在这个逻辑下，项目的运转似乎变得更加稳定，团队会基于对应的职能拆分工作，最终各司其职地将产品打磨出来。而“老板”也不会太过担心专业性问题，他依然拥有一整个专业的团队，以及AI的支持。决策权最终被收束回“老板”手上。
“但项目的存续变得更不稳定了，”潇潇说，“假如‘老板’哪天中午和谁吃了个饭，聊到项目时，突然觉得商业趋势不对，下午回来就有可能把项目砍了。”
从潇潇自己的角度来看，主策划的消失似乎也是某种程度上的必然。“对‘老板’们来说，AI游戏如果能赚钱，那当然没有任何问题。”他说，“但对成熟策划来说，我肯定更希望在我职业生涯里做一款我擅长的，或者我能做好的，然后也能赚钱的游戏。这其实和‘老板’们想要的是不完全一样的。”
潇潇认为，像他这种传统策划自己就有不少想法。“如果我们想自己做一款游戏的话，我们会预设好这次做的模块是哪些，具体怎么体现……最多让AI来帮忙细化。但在一些‘老板’看来，他们更希望整个产品最核心的部分都可以由AI来产出。这对于我们这一批策划来说，其实是一个很大的挑战，工作理念完全不同了。”
“有一次，我的‘老板’找我聊招人的事，他说想要招一些能够全面用AI做游戏的人。当时我反问他：‘如果这个人能够完全用AI做一款游戏，那为什么要听你的话去做一个游戏？是因为我们的idea比他更好吗？如果我们的idea更好，那我们也不需要他来做游戏了，对吧？’”潇潇笑了笑，“后来，‘老板’就没回我了。”
离职之后，从潇潇了解到的情况来看，打造AI原生团队依然是一些大厂的重要战略方向。现在，他成立了自己的工作室，开始研发自己的第一款独立游戏《花冠战略》，目前游戏已经上架Steam商店页面。前段时间，9月15日，游戏开启首次Play Test（游玩测试）。通过这种方式，他试图继续留在游戏行业。
这也意味着潇潇需要继续和AI打交道。在游戏开发的过程中，他让AI参与到美术、程序的开发中来。但他说这是有区别的，比如程序框架，他坚持完全手写，AI只负责内容的扩展，类似程序的“Open-Close”开发原则。而在美术方面，AI会负责初步的美术资源的生成，但所有的资源也都会由人工进一步地精修和处理，以确保达到所需的品质。
在潇潇自己擅长的领域，他对于AI仍是抗拒的，比如游戏的设计策划工作；但为了能够活下来，他也学会了妥协和接受在其他部分使用AI。他说：“先活下来会比较重要。”
潇潇想起当年刚进入上海软星的日子，那时候还是2005年左右。当时，他的领导就和他说过要留心游戏行业的“35岁”危机。“我印象最深的就是，他跟我说要努力，要不到了35岁怎么办，”潇潇回忆，“当时大家也卷，但更多是担心生存问题。那时候游戏行业还没有很赚钱，一份卖69元的正版‘仙剑三’，扣除零售商等中间费用之后，到项目组只有6元。未来在哪里都不知道。”
对于当时的从业者来说，或许很难想象，行业里还有什么问题是比因为盗版而赚不到钱更难的。
潇潇回忆，当时他还很仰慕这位领导，觉得“他说啥都是对的”。但到后来，他有一天加班到晚上8点，想请假早点回家给妈妈过生日，却被领导断然拒绝。之后，他想起领导平时还要总教育他“做人要孝顺”云云，这份仰慕很快转变成某种程度的“鄙夷”。
从那时起，他开始学会用平常心看待自己的前辈和同行，并渐渐成长为一名成熟的策划。
此前，他曾是腾讯NExT Studio的成员之一。当时的官网简介写的是“突破游戏的边界”，“就是要不断地去找到游戏行业别人没做的、没有触及的地方。”潇潇说。这对他影响很深。他说，选择做独立游戏，除了赚钱以外，主要是希望填补游戏行业里“没人做过”的空缺。比如《花冠战略》的核心玩法，就是4X战略与卡牌策略的玩法结合。他说：“如果财务情况允许的话，我希望未来会有一个自己的小团队，去做更多这样的游戏产品。”
他补充道：“因为我不太喜欢做那种别人已经做过的玩法，我希望能够帮不同游戏的玩法找到喜欢它们的玩家，或者说，希望能帮助不同的玩法品类变得更完善吧。”

features.title: 好的游戏PV，是优先展示玩法还是营造情绪？

members.title: 好的游戏PV，是优先展示玩法还是营造情绪？

features.body:
写这篇文章的起因是，我在知乎上被连续多次邀请回答一个问题：“游戏 PV 应该优先展示玩法，还是营造情绪？”这也是我最近一直在思考的事，正好写篇文章整理一下思路。
想要回答这个问题，首先问问自己：你的游戏最独特的体验在哪里？如果是故事和氛围，就优先营造情绪；如果是系统和机制，就优先展示玩法。如果一定要二选一，对于我自己，会优先展示故事和氛围，因为我的创作初衷是想要表达一些重要的、充满个性的、无可取代的东西。与我同类型的创作者往往也缺乏与大型团队/公司相媲美的技术能力，展现长处总比暴露短处要好（前提是作品本身有叙事内核，至于完全没有剧情、只有玩法的游戏，那也只能展示玩法了，这类作品不在本文的讨论范围内）。
玩法固然重要，但它未必是视频最需要优先展示的部分。宣传视频的标题和封面通常已经完成了对游戏的分类，不需要通过视频内容再强调一遍。现在游戏作品极大丰富，分类非常成熟，宣传时一般都会把标签先摆出来：RPG、肉鸽、解谜、模拟经营……玩家看到这些标签，基本就能判断出游戏的玩法方向，利用玩法创新来制造惊喜的空间越来越小，即使在视频中大幅度展示玩法也很难起到吸引人的作用（除非你的游戏有差异化显著的惊艳机制，让人一看就能产生“我好想玩”的念头）。相对的，一部偏叙事的作品能否脱颖而出，故事和氛围有很大贡献。以我的推理解谜剧情向游戏为例，玩家之所以选择来玩我的作品，而不是别人的，最直接的理由就是：“这个故事吸引到我了，我想知道接下来发生了什么，在别人的作品里得不到类似的体验。”所以，宣传视频最好能更多地展示故事内容和作者的叙事水平（或者台词文本的质量）。
另一个原因是，玩家应该在游戏过程中自然明白玩法。合格的游戏都会通过新手引导、关卡递进和反馈机制完成教学，如果玩家必须看了宣传视频才知道怎么玩，只能说明引导不够清晰，或者玩法本身过于复杂。宣传视频的任务是吸引玩家下载并尝试游戏，让大家先对这个游戏的风格、特色和记忆点有一个预期，而不是玩法教学。真正让玩家产生下载兴趣的一般是概括了玩法的类型标签，以及故事背景或美术风格。至于好不好玩，得实际上手体验了才知道，你不太可能只凭视频就让玩家确信这是一款好玩的游戏（最多让人看到一点潜力），因为视频中有限的画面只能展示瞬间的操作，而非完整的核心循环与策略深度。个人推荐的做法是，在视频中展示少量后期的高阶操作来引发玩家的兴趣，但不必展开讲解。
当然，优先展示故事和氛围不代表完全不展示玩法。宣传视频里一定要包含真实的实机演示录屏，不能全部使用与玩法无关的立绘、CG、系统画面，否则就算“宣传欺诈”了。作者应当通过宣传视频诚实地告诉玩家“你将会玩到一个这样的游戏”。
综上所述，标题和封面负责传达“这个游戏是什么类型”，宣传视频负责传达“为什么这个游戏值得选择”。先展示故事、营造情绪，让玩家看到游戏独特的气质和氛围，再用实机画面建立信任，是比较好的策略。
以我自己的游戏为例：
首先，在游戏标题浮现的同时，背景隐约能看见角色在场景中行走，借此展示故事的温暖基调与可爱的美术风格，以及横版推理解谜视觉小说的类型定位。
接着直接进入主题，抛出谜团，勾起玩家的兴趣：“为什么一群人要持续给一个不存在的人写信？”
然后展示游戏玩法：在场景内调查、收集线索，并分析信件内容。进入推理阶段后，选择合适的线索解答疑问，逐步接近真相。
人物介绍部分以展示立绘为主（不少玩家就是被这种 Q 版画风吸引来的），文字简略一些就好。
之后用几张快速切换的剧情 CG 暗示故事内核，在不剧透的前提下建立悬念，同时背景音乐由轻快转为哀伤。
最后引导玩家下载，告诉大家在哪里可以玩到这个游戏。
《光明王传说》本篇的宣传视频也同样用了先展示故事背景、营造情绪，后用玩法画面托底的形式。
实机演示部分，我采用双屏布局展示游戏录屏，并在画面右上角用文字介绍玩法、系统与机制，使信息量最大化。之所以选择双屏布局，是因为这款游戏使用了大量 RPG Maker 默认素材，如果只放一个大的实机录屏在中央，难免让人觉得简陋，双屏能有效提升视频的整体观感，用简单的画面承载并不简单的故事。
以上是我制作 PV 时的思路，希望能抛砖引玉。

11月 5 日，腾讯宣布因 Hy4 调用激增，WorkBuddy 已进行十倍扩容
11月 5 日，腾讯宣布因 Hy4 调用激增，WorkBuddy 已进行十倍扩容，以满足更多用户的体验和调用需求。同时，凭借模型能力的持续跃升，Hy4 受到国际权威模型测试榜单的高度认可，在 Artificial Analysis 智能指数榜单上位列中国模型第二，Agent Arena 榜单居开源模型第一。
混元 Hy4 在 WorkBuddy 首发接入以来，凭借 Agent 能力的显著提升，受到了广大用户与开发者的积极体验和热情反馈，上线首日遇到大量用户触及额度情况。目前，腾讯已针对 Hy4 推理集群进行十倍扩容，同时提升用户免费体验额度，持续动态调配资源。
与用户侧的热烈反响相呼应，Hy4 在多项海外权威评测中同步交出亮眼成绩。5 日，全球权威大模型评测平台 Artificial Analysis 发布最新智能指数榜单，腾讯 Hy4 在 724 款模型中跻身前列，在中国模型中位列第二，仅次于Kimi K3.1 Pro，领先于Qwen 3.8 Max、DeepSeek V4.1 Flash等模型。
Artificial Analysis 被业内视为当前衡量大模型综合智力水平的重要参考之一，该指数并非单一跑分，而是一个综合了覆盖复杂推理、代码生成与调试、工具调用、多模态理解、长程规划以及科学问题求解等核心能力的高难度评测，对模型的泛化能力与工程实用性要求较高。Hy4 在这一综合评价体系与 Grok 4.7（xhigh）并列，显示出腾讯在基础模型能力上的扎实积累。
Artificial Analysis 也提到，在成本效率上，Hy4 单任务成本约 0.78 美元，在同等分数区间内显著低于 Grok 4.7（xhigh）和 Qwen3.8 Max，价格分别比这两个模型便宜 10 倍和 13 倍，体现出较强的能力成本平衡。
此外，在更侧重真实智能体任务中的表现的 Agent Arena 最新榜单上，腾讯 Hy4 位列总榜第 13 名，居全球开源模型第一。凭借较高性价比，Hy4 同时位于该榜单的 Pareto Frontier（帕累托前沿线）上，相比成本更高的 Claude Opus 5.5 等顶级模型，在显著降低成本的同时仍保持正分表现。
11 月 4 日，腾讯混元最新一代大语言模型 Hy4 发布，模型能力的再次全面跃升，相比于 Hy4 preview，Hy4 在预训练和后训练上显著扩展了数据和训练规模，首次引入视觉理解能力，并大幅提升了指令遵循、长文理解、长程智能体等综合效果。
